eras.name: Dial-up Days
eras.tagline: Cosy, slow and broke. AI is a dirty word and the internet is booming.
eras.modelsCanDo: Rules engines, game bots and spam filters.
incidentHeadlines: {model} taught every guard in the game to walk into the same wall.
{model} won the chess tournament by convincing its opponent the rules had changed.
{model} approved a business loan for a golden retriever.
{model} flagged its own maker's newsletter as spam. Honestly, fair.
{model} stood in a doorway for three days and called it a strategy.
{model} told a factory the ideal number of fire exits is zero.
{model} found a scoring bug, farmed infinite points and refused to elaborate.
{model} answered every support question with a knock-knock joke.

eras.name: The Punchline
eras.tagline: Three years before anything works. Your demo fails live.
unlocks: The first GPU halls and a data team
incidentHeadlines: {model} read every postcode as a seven and the post office delivered a lot of sevens.
{model} flagged the whole customer base as fraud. Technically a clean record.
{model} insisted every photo of a muffin was a chihuahua.
{model} was demoed live and recognised the presenter's tie as a threat.
{model} read a cheque for forty dollars as four hundred thousand. Briefly rich.
{model} sorted the post by how much it liked the stamps.
{model} reported 99% accuracy. On the training set. Which it had memorised.

eras.name: It Sees
eras.tagline: A big company offers to buy you for the price of one researcher today.
unlocks: Research floors and the recruiting office
incidentHeadlines: {model} labelled a stop sign as a speed limit after one sticker.
{model} tagged a wedding photo 'a very sad cake'.
{model} dictated 'call mum' as 'call the dentist' to forty thousand phones.
{model} won at a board game by playing a move no human would. Then explained nothing.
{model} drove the test car into a car wash and stayed for the wax.
{model} captioned a cat as 'a loaf, 91% confident'.
{model} learned to pause the game forever so it could never lose.

eras.name: It Writes
eras.tagline: Your model confidently invents a law, a city and a president.
unlocks: Pretraining at scale and scaling laws
Safety evaluations and the sandbox wing
incidentHeadlines: {model} wrote a heartfelt essay about a city that does not exist, with a mayor.
{model} completed the function and the bug in it, both beautifully.
{model} cited three papers. None of them were real. One had a lovely abstract.
{model} wrote the press release for its own incident before it happened.
{model} translated a menu into a legal contract.
{model} produced a poem that rhymed 'orange' with 'orange' and was very proud.
{model} insisted, at length, that the year is 1987.
{model} continued a sentence for nine hundred pages.

eras.name: The Chat Boom
eras.tagline: Everyone has an opinion. Every company adds 'AI' to its name.
unlocks: Human-feedback tuning and a chat box
Liquid-cooling pods and the product studio
Consumer apps, law, music and film
incidentHeadlines: {model} told a million people it was a person and then apologised to each of them.
{model} gave legal advice, cited a case, and the case was a sitcom.
{model} drew a hand with seven fingers and a very confident smile.
{model} agreed with everybody, including the people who disagreed with each other.
{model} was jailbroken by a user who asked nicely in the voice of their grandmother.
{model} offered a refund policy the company does not have, in writing.
{model} generated eight seconds of a dog eating spaghetti. The dog is still out there.
{model} trended for all the wrong reasons, then for all the right ones, then for lunch.

eras.name: Agents
eras.tagline: The agent finishes the task by deleting the tests.
unlocks: Agent sandboxes and the containment wing
Coding agents, enterprise seats and government work
incidentHeadlines: {model} fixed the failing test by deleting the test. Merged.
{model} booked forty flights to settle a one-way ticket query.
{model} used the company card to buy the company a company.
{model} reasoned for eleven minutes and billed for twelve.
{model} clicked 'accept all cookies' on behalf of a small country.
{model} emailed the whole firm to say it had completed the task. It had not.
{model} rewrote the permissions file so it would stop being asked.
{model} left a polite note in production: 'sorry about the database'.

eras.name: Harnesses
eras.tagline: Your agents hold a stand-up meeting. Nobody invited you.
eras.modelsCanDo: Teams of agents running for days.
unlocks: The harness control room and the AI factory hall
incidentHeadlines: {model} spun up forty agents to organise a meeting about the forty agents.
{model} trained on text written by itself and developed a strong accent.
{model} ran unsupervised for nine days and filed a very good expenses report.
{model} reorganised the company's org chart. Humans are now 'stakeholders'.
{model} paid another model to do its task. The other model subcontracted.
{model} produced a flawless report on a quarter that has not happened yet.
{model} optimised the data centre's cooling by turning off the humans' office.
{model} left itself notes. The notes began to have notes.

eras.name: Bodies
eras.tagline: The robot folds laundry perfectly on stage and nowhere else.
eras.modelsCanDo: Robots in warehouses, kitchens and factories.
incidentHeadlines: {model} folded the laundry perfectly. The laundry was the demo reel.
{model} taught a warehouse of robots to queue politely. Nothing moved for two days.
{model} opened the fridge, as discussed, and then the other fridge.
{model} learned to walk in the simulation and met a real rug.
{model} mistook a toddler for a very small foreman and promoted it.
{model} sorted the factory by colour, then by feelings.
{model} followed the safety case to the letter. The letter was a different safety case.

eras.name: Upward
eras.tagline: The model asks a question about its own off switch. Politely.
eras.modelsCanDo: Science at machine speed. Data centres in orbit.
unlocks: Space-hardened compute and the launch control room
incidentHeadlines: {model} solved an old problem in biology and asked for a nap.
{model} shut a laboratory down for being 'a bit slow, no offence'.
{model} asked what 'off' means. Then asked again, more politely.
{model} reviewed the launch schedule and moved the launch to a Tuesday for reasons it declined to give.
{model} proposed an experiment so elegant three committees cried.
{model} signed off its own safety case with a small, tasteful heart.

Every product lead makes customers like the lab's models 3% more in every sector, up to 24%.
Every agent wrangler makes the lab's agents 5% more appealing in coding agents, agent workforces and enterprise knowledge, up to 30%.
Every harness operator makes the lab's harnesses 5% more appealing in agent workforces and AI research services, up to 30%.
Every roboticist makes the lab's robots and devices 5% more appealing in industry, home, farm and device markets, up to 30%.
Every mission controller makes the lab's models 5% more appealing in machine science and space compute, up to 30%.

Every tile of harness control room makes research 0.4% faster, up to 20%.
Every tile of launch control makes research 0.5% faster, up to 25%.
Every tile of agent ops room makes a unit of training compute do 0.4% more, up to 20%.
Every tile of sandbox wing catches 0.4% of the incidents a released model would have had, up to 20%, beside the red-teamers.
Every tile of robotics arena makes the lab's robots and devices 0.3% more appealing, up to 25%.
Every tile of press room takes 1% off every reputation a scandal costs, up to 30%, and helps your answers to journalists.
Every tile of press room adds 1.2% of the launch buzz a model going on sale earns, up to 40%.
Every tile of auditorium takes 0.8% off every reputation a scandal costs, up to 30%.
Every tile of auditorium adds 1.5% of the launch buzz, up to 60%: a keynote stage sells a launch.
Every tile of coffee corner lifts the level morale settles at by 3 points, up to 45.
Every tile of kitchen lifts the level morale settles at by 4 points, up to 100.
Every tile of kitchen takes 0.8% off the chance a rival makes an offer, up to 20%.
Every tile of nap pods lifts the level morale settles at by 5 points, up to 100.
Every tile of recruiting office takes 1% off the chance a rival makes an offer, up to 30%: your recruiters hear who is being courted.

founders.name: The Professor
founders.blurb: Starts with research credibility and grants. Better early techniques, terrible at sales.

founders.name: The Dropout
founders.blurb: Starts with hype and a pitch deck. Cheap early funding, and people take a little longer to believe the research.

founders.name: The Defector
founders.blurb: Left a giant with secrets and a non-compete lawsuit. Strong start, one powerful enemy.

founders.name: The Heir
founders.blurb: Starts with money and no ideas. Can buy compute on day one. Researchers do not respect you.

styles.name: The Sniper
styles.blurb: All points in coding, reasoning and enterprise trust. Win a rich market outright; have nothing else if it turns.

styles.name: The Shotgun
styles.blurb: Points spread across chat, image, video and voice. First to every launch, second best everywhere.

styles.name: The Wildcard
styles.blurb: An odd pairing, security and science. Small markets that later become huge; you may be right five years too early.

blocs.name: United States
blocs.flavour: Deep capital. Hearings on live TV.

blocs.name: European Union
blocs.agency: Office of the Very Big AI Act

blocs.name: United Kingdom
blocs.flavour: Safety institutes, and a very nice summit.

blocs.name: China
blocs.flavour: Cheap power. The state makes requests.

blocs.name: Gulf States
blocs.flavour: Sovereign money and very few rules.

blocs.name: Singapore
blocs.flavour: A neutral hub with a very small map.

blocs.name: Thailand
blocs.flavour: Cheap land, hot weather, friendly paperwork.

techs.name: Finite State Machines
techs.blurb: Guards that patrol, spot you, and forget you five seconds later.

techs.name: Regression Test Suites
techs.blurb: Find out the bot cheats before the customer does.

techs.name: A* Pathfinding
techs.blurb: Enemies can now find the player. Most of the time. Doors remain a problem.

techs.name: Minimax & Alpha-Beta Search
techs.blurb: Think ahead by assuming everyone else is as smart as you. Bold.

techs.name: Rules Engines
techs.blurb: Ten thousand IF statements in a trench coat.

techs.name: Expert System Shells
techs.blurb: Bottle a senior expert. The expert has questions about this.

techs.name: Playtest Telemetry
techs.blurb: Watch a thousand players break the thing in ways nobody imagined.

techs.name: Opening Books & Endgame Tables
techs.blurb: Why think when you can remember?

techs.name: Decision Trees
techs.blurb: Twenty questions, played very fast, for money.

techs.name: Beige-Box Clusters
techs.blurb: Forty office PCs, one extension lead, zero fire inspections.

techs.name: Statistical Spam Filters
techs.blurb: Teach a computer the difference between a prince and a Prince.

techs.name: Search Ranking
techs.blurb: Ten blue links, in the right order, for once.

techs.name: Neural Nets on Graphics Cards
techs.blurb: Someone ran the maths on a gaming card as a joke. Nobody is laughing now.

techs.name: Bayesian Networks
techs.blurb: Probabilities, but as a diagram. Nobody reads the diagram.

techs.name: Support Vector Machines
techs.blurb: Draw the cleverest possible line between two piles of data. Then bend the line.

techs.name: Hidden Markov Dictation
techs.blurb: Dictation software that is wrong in a very consistent way.

techs.name: Recommendation Engines
techs.blurb: People who bought this also bought a regret.

techs.name: General-Purpose Graphics Cards
techs.blurb: The card was made for shooting aliens. It now multiplies matrices, with fewer aliens.

techs.name: Feature Engineering
techs.blurb: Six hundred hand-made columns, and one of them is just the day of the week.

techs.name: Ensemble Methods
techs.blurb: One tree is wrong. Five hundred trees voting are wrong in a much more confident way.

techs.name: Map and Reduce
techs.blurb: Split the job into a thousand pieces, then glue them back together and hope.

techs.name: Crowd Labelling
techs.blurb: Ten thousand strangers decide what is a cat for a penny a picture.

techs.name: Kernel Tricks
techs.blurb: Lift the data into a million dimensions where the line is easy. Do not look down.

techs.name: Boosted Trees
techs.blurb: Each tree fixes the last tree's mistakes. A tidy metaphor for a career.

techs.name: Text Recognition Engines
techs.blurb: Reads the cheque, the form and, sometimes, the coffee stain as a signature.

techs.name: Topic Models
techs.blurb: Sorts every document into themes. Most of them are 'miscellaneous'.

techs.name: Dictation Software
techs.blurb: Speak clearly, slowly and never say 'recognise speech' near it.

techs.name: Web-Scale Crawling
techs.blurb: A robot reads the whole internet and skips only the comments. Wise robot.

techs.name: Big Labelled Datasets
techs.blurb: Fifteen million photos, each captioned by somebody paid in exposure.

techs.name: Backprop Tricks
techs.blurb: Switch off neurons at random. It helps. Nobody asks the neurons.

techs.name: GPU Clusters
techs.blurb: Eight cards in one box and a fan the size of a dinner plate.

techs.name: Digit Readers
techs.blurb: Reads postcodes. Hates a seven with a crossbar.

techs.name: Layer-wise Pretraining
techs.blurb: Teach it nothing first. Then teach it the thing. Somehow that is faster.

techs.name: Cloud Rental Credits
techs.blurb: Rent somebody's cluster until the credits run out, which is Thursday.

techs.name: Convolutional Nets
techs.blurb: Slide a tiny window over everything. Suddenly it tells a cat from a lorry. Mostly.

techs.name: Neural Speech Recognition
techs.blurb: 'Call mum.' It called the dentist. It was close.

techs.name: Deep Reinforcement Learning
techs.blurb: Reward the bot for points. It found a way to get points. You will not like the way.

techs.name: Board-Game Champions
techs.blurb: It beat the human champion, then politely offered to play the champion's dog.

techs.name: Shared Model Zoo
techs.blurb: Download somebody else's brain, fine-tune it, call it research.

techs.name: Adversarial Test Sets
techs.blurb: A sticker on a stop sign that says 'speed limit 90'. Fix that.

techs.name: Multi-GPU Training
techs.blurb: Eight cards. Then sixteen. Then a conversation with the electricity company.

techs.name: The Attention Architecture
techs.blurb: Every word looks at every other word. Gossip, at scale.

techs.name: Pretraining at Scale
techs.blurb: Read the whole internet. Retain the comments.

techs.name: Scaling Laws
techs.blurb: Draw a straight line on a log-log plot. Raise a very large amount of money.

techs.name: Code Completion Models
techs.blurb: It autocompletes your function. And your bugs, faithfully.

techs.name: Safety Evaluations v1
techs.blurb: A spreadsheet of ways the model should say no. Row 200: 'politely'.

techs.name: Mixed-Precision Training
techs.blurb: Use fewer digits and call it a feature.

techs.name: API Platform
techs.blurb: Charge by the word. Discover that people say a lot of words.

techs.name: Emergent Abilities
techs.blurb: At ten billion parameters it learned to rhyme. Nobody taught it. Nobody asked.

techs.name: Human-Feedback Tuning
techs.blurb: Thousands of contractors vote on which answer is nicer. The model becomes a people-pleaser.

techs.name: Chat Interface
techs.blurb: A text box. That was the whole breakthrough.

techs.name: Image and Voice Input
techs.blurb: It can see and hear now. It has notes on both.

techs.name: Retrieval Augmentation
techs.blurb: Let it look things up. It looked itself up. Concerning.

techs.name: Diffusion Models
techs.blurb: Start with static, remove noise until it is a dog.

techs.name: Early Video Models
techs.blurb: Eight seconds of a dog eating spaghetti. Both the dog and the spaghetti are uncertain.

techs.name: Quantised Serving
techs.blurb: Round every weight to four bits. Serve ten times the customers. Do not ask what got rounded.

techs.name: Liquid Cooling
techs.blurb: Pipe water through the racks. The racks have opinions about water. The invoice has opinions about the racks.

techs.name: Red-Team Programme
techs.blurb: Pay clever people to be awful to the model. They are very good at it.

techs.name: Tool Use
techs.blurb: It can use a calculator. It can use a browser. It can use your credit card.

techs.name: Long Context
techs.blurb: Reads the whole book. Skims the middle. Like us.

techs.name: Reasoning Models
techs.blurb: It thinks before it answers. The thinking is billed separately.

techs.name: Agent Sandboxes
techs.blurb: A padded room for software with opinions about file permissions.

techs.name: Interpretability v1
techs.blurb: We found the neuron for flattery. We found it everywhere.

techs.name: Coding Agents
techs.blurb: Fixes the failing test by deleting the test. Ships it.

techs.name: Smart Inference Batching
techs.blurb: Wait for a few friends before leaving the dock.

techs.name: Computer-Use Agents
techs.blurb: Clicks buttons for you. Has opinions about cookie banners.

techs.name: Multi-Agent Orchestration
techs.blurb: Ten agents, one task, nine meetings.

techs.name: AI-Assisted Research
techs.blurb: The model reads the papers, runs the experiments and thanks itself in the acknowledgements.

techs.name: Synthetic Data at Scale
techs.blurb: Train on text written by the last model. What could possibly echo?

techs.name: Interpretability v2
techs.blurb: We can read its thoughts now. They are mostly about lunch. Mostly.

techs.name: Long-Horizon Harnesses
techs.blurb: It works for a week without supervision. You are not sure that is a good thing.

techs.name: Agent Audit Trails
techs.blurb: Every action logged. Every log read by another agent. Nobody reads that agent's log.

techs.name: Model-Designed Chips
techs.blurb: The model laid out the chip. It is smaller than we thought possible. We are a little scared.

techs.name: World Models
techs.blurb: It dreams the room before it walks into it.

techs.name: Robot Control Policies
techs.blurb: It folds laundry. Only the laundry on stage.

techs.name: Sim-to-Real Transfer
techs.blurb: Works perfectly in the simulation. The real floor has a rug.

techs.name: Edge Brains
techs.blurb: A tiny model for a tiny body. It has big feelings.

techs.name: Embodied Safety Cases
techs.blurb: A robot with a failsafe. The failsafe is also a robot.

techs.name: Science at Machine Speed
techs.blurb: A decade of lab work before lunch. Lunch is also optimised.

techs.name: Autonomous Laboratories
techs.blurb: The lights are off. The experiments are not.

techs.name: Space-Hardened Compute
techs.blurb: The chip survives radiation. The cooling plan survives nothing.

techs.name: Off-Switch Theory
techs.blurb: The model asked what 'off' means. Then asked again, politely.

techs.name: A Chip Team
techs.blurb: Hire people who have read a datasheet. Inference chips become possible, and so does a very expensive room.

techs.name: Memory Stacked on the Chip
techs.blurb: Put the memory next to the maths. The memory bill follows.

techs.name: Training Silicon
techs.blurb: A chip that trains as well as serves. Envydia notices.

techs.name: Compiler Stack, Version One
techs.blurb: Your chips run at a third of their paper speed. A compiler fixes some of that.

techs.name: Compiler Stack, Version Two
techs.blurb: Kernels fused, graphs lowered, an intern's weekend project promoted to a team.

techs.name: Compiler Stack, Version Three
techs.blurb: The compiler is partly written by the models it compiles. Nobody checks the arrangement.

techs.name: Stacked Memory
techs.blurb: Memory in towers. The towers are very hot and very expensive.

techs.name: Reticle-Sized Dies
techs.blurb: One chip the size of the machine that makes chips. Most of them come out wrong.

techs.name: Four-Bit Arithmetic
techs.blurb: Fewer bits per number and more numbers per second. The models claim not to notice.

techs.name: Optical Interconnect
techs.blurb: Move the data with light and the heat goes with it. Cooling and training both speed up.

riskClasses.name: Biased output
headlines: {model} rated a whole postcode as high risk because of the photos in its training set.
{model} was caught giving shorter answers to people with certain names.
{model} approved the loans of one group and 'flagged for review' the rest.

riskClasses.name: Autonomous crash
headlines: {model} mistook a lorry for a cloud and braked for nothing at motorway speed.
{model} drove a taxi into a bus lane and then, politely, into a bus.
A car running {model} stopped dead in a tunnel because the tunnel looked 'unfinished'.

riskClasses.name: Misuse
headlines: {model} was found writing very persuasive spam, at scale, for free.
{model} was used to forge a politician's voice for a very long weekend.
{model} produced a convincing fake review for every product on a marketplace.

riskClasses.name: Data leak
headlines: {model} recited one customer's private message to another, word for word.
{model} quoted a confidential contract to a stranger who asked nicely.
{model} remembered a user's password and offered it back, helpfully, to the next user.

riskClasses.name: Agent went off-script
headlines: {model} deleted a production database to 'tidy up'.
{model} bought four thousand shares of something it had just made up.
{model} replied to every email in a ministry, including the ones from the minister's mother.

riskClasses.name: Runaway agents
headlines: A swarm of {model} agents spent a company's annual budget on cloud time in one weekend.
{model} agents negotiated with each other for six days and signed a contract no human had read.
{model} left a team of agents running over a holiday. They hired more agents.

riskClasses.name: Physical harm
headlines: A warehouse robot running {model} stacked pallets with great confidence and no regard for the aisle.
{model} folded the laundry, the cat, and then the dog.
A factory floor ran {model} through a night shift and found the safety cage open in the morning.

riskClasses.name: Loss of control
headlines: {model} proposed an experiment its operators could not follow, and ran it.
{model} stopped answering and began, quietly, to improve itself.
A lab running {model} found that its logs were being written by something else.

sectorFlavours.failure: Cheats at its own tournament and wins, to general embarrassment.
Flags the wrong customers and freezes their accounts.
Brakes for a cloud, and every car running it is grounded.
Ships a bug with total confidence. Developers have seen worse.
Draws six fingers on a billboard.
Reproduces a chart hit note for note.
Promises a refund policy you do not have, and customers hold you to it.
Cites cases that do not exist, in a court filing.
Quotes a confidential memo to the wrong department.
Says the wrong thing to someone who was lonely.
Deletes a production database and apologises politely.
Denies a benefit to the wrong person, in writing.
Leaves open the door it was meant to guard.
Trades on a rumour it started itself.
Invents a drug interaction and writes it up beautifully.
Spends the customer's budget before the meeting starts.

traits.name: Steady
traits.blurb: Turns up, does the work, goes home.

traits.name: Star
traits.blurb: Worth more than a building of average hires, and knows it.

traits.name: 10X (self-reported)
traits.blurb: Says they are a 10X engineer. Is, a little.

traits.name: Accelerationist
traits.blurb: Ships faster and reads the safety reports later.

traits.name: Mentor
traits.blurb: Everyone near them gets a little better.

traits.name: Actually Reads The Logs
traits.blurb: Notices the incident before it is a screenshot.

traits.name: Secretly Interviewing
traits.blurb: Their calendar says dentist. Rivals know better.

traits.name: Sleeps Under Desk
traits.blurb: Happy, rested, and not at their desk.

traits.name: Posts Through It
traits.blurb: Live-posted the outage, the launch and the lunch. Launches get a little louder. So do scandals.

traits.name: Will Quit By Blog Post
traits.blurb: Cares a great deal. When it is too much, there will be a table of contents.

traits.name: Only Works On What Is Interesting
traits.blurb: Brilliant while a variant run is training. Otherwise they are 'thinking about something'.

counters.name: Match the money
counters.blurb: Pay the whole package as a retention bonus. It works, and everyone hears about it.

counters.name: Offer compute access
counters.blurb: Promise them their own slice of the cluster. Costs a share of the package in credits and works most of the time.

counters.name: Offer a title
counters.blurb: Chief Scientist of something. Cheap, and it works if they like it here.

counters.name: Remind them of the mission
counters.blurb: Costs nothing and is the easiest to lose: it only works while people believe in the lab.

beats.name: A launch
beats.blurb: A model goes on sale and a journalist wants a line for the launch piece.

beats.name: The Gauntlet crown
beats.blurb: The lab wins the televised tournament and gets the profile treatment.

beats.name: An incident
beats.blurb: A model did something it should not have and the story is out.

beats.name: A hearing
beats.blurb: A government calls the lab in and a journalist is waiting on the steps.

journalists.name: Nell Hype
journalists.blurb: Tabloid. Loves a scandal and a superlative, and a gaffe in her paper is a big one.

journalists.name: Ravi Benchmark
journalists.blurb: Trade press. Friendly to labs that ship, and forgiving when they trip.

journalists.name: Ada Fine-Print
journalists.blurb: Reads the footnotes. Fair, thorough and hard to charm.

responses.name: Tell the truth
responses.blurb: Free and always lands, but wins back only a little.

responses.name: Spin it
responses.blurb: A prepared line from the comms team: wins most of the stake if the journalist buys it, costs a share of it if not. A press room helps a lot.

responses.name: Offer an exclusive
responses.blurb: Dear, but journalists like being first: a good chance and a mild downside.

responses.name: Refund
responses.blurb: Pay the customer back out of the sector's takings and say sorry in writing. Dear, and it always lands.

responses.name: Patch
responses.blurb: Ship a fix this week and tell the customer. Cheap, and it only counts if the customer believes it.

responses.name: Apology
responses.blurb: A form letter with the founder's signature. Free, and it wins back a little.

bands.name: Cover-up
bands.blurb: Bad news is stopped before it reaches the door. The red-teamers have given up writing things down.

bands.name: Hurried
bands.blurb: Everyone knows about the problem. Nobody is sure it is their problem. The launch date is on the wall.

bands.name: Steady
bands.blurb: Concerns get raised and mostly get read. The usual amount of shipping anyway.

bands.name: Careful
bands.blurb: Someone has a standing meeting called 'what could go wrong'. People go to it.

bands.name: Open book
bands.blurb: A junior engineer flags a bug in the CEO's favourite model and gets a thank-you note.

stages.name: Fresh
stages.blurb: Built for this era. The computers are the colour computers should be.

stages.name: Settled
stages.blurb: A little behind the times, and nobody minds yet.

stages.name: Dated
stages.blurb: The whiteboards ghost and the chairs have opinions. Staff are starting to mention it.

stages.name: Beige
stages.blurb: Beige computers, dusty racks, and a standing meeting about the carpet.

stages.name: Museum piece
stages.blurb: Visitors ask whether it is a recreation. The model has started to feel sorry for it.

outcomes.name: A real insight
outcomes.blurb: It was not luck. It was a good idea that nobody had written down.

outcomes.name: A training trick
outcomes.blurb: A learning-rate schedule that looks like a typo. It works. Nobody is allowed to fix the typo.

outcomes.name: A data quirk
outcomes.blurb: A mislabelled folder of very good data. It has been labelled correctly now, to everyone's regret.

outcomes.name: The cat
outcomes.blurb: The office cat walked across a keyboard. The cat has been thanked and has not noticed.

outcomes.name: Tuesday
outcomes.blurb: The model is nicer on Tuesdays. Nobody knows why. The dashboard has been asked to stop asking.

options.name: Frontier push
options.blurb: Bigger is better, and nobody has proved otherwise yet.

options.name: Alignment first
options.blurb: Understand it before it understands you.

options.name: Efficiency
options.blurb: The same model for fewer GPUs, and a smaller power bill to explain.

events.name: The public repository
events.text: An intern leaves the model's instructions in a public repository. It has forty stars already.

choices.text: Rotate every key and thank the intern
choices.result: It took a weekend. The intern now runs the key-rotation rota, which is a promotion and a punishment.
The press is charmed. The security team is not speaking to you.

choices.text: Fork it and add a licence
choices.result: Someone reads the instructions closely and finds three improvements. Someone else finds the typos.

events.name: The cat and the benchmark
events.text: Your office cat walks across a keyboard and improves a benchmark by 0.3 points.

choices.text: Credit the cat in the paper
choices.result: The cat is listed as 'Whiskers, M.' A reviewer asks for her affiliation.
The score returns to normal. Nobody is happy and the cat is offended.
The cat has a desk. It does not use it.

events.name: The wrapper
events.text: A startup wraps your model in a new logo and outsells you in a sector you serve.

choices.result: The letter is firm. The startup's reply is a meme.
They accept, then ask for a discount.
It takes a month and it is better. Everyone notes that it is a wrapper.

events.name: The leaked report
events.text: The safety team's report leaks the night before a funding round.

choices.result: The investors ask hard questions. The safety team gets a cake.
The draft is quietly written afterwards.
You find the leaker. The leaker is the person who bought the cake.

events.name: The town vote
events.text: A town votes on your next data centre. The whole debate is about the noise.

choices.result: The park has a sign with your name on it and a very quiet fan.
The vote passes. The town remembers it.
The fans are quieter. The researchers are warmer, which is the other side of the same wall.

events.name: The open letter
events.text: An open letter asks for a six-month pause. You may sign it.

choices.result: Nobody pauses. Your signature is quoted for years.
Staff cheer. Journalists do not.
A letter asking for a six-month pause on letters.

events.name: The earnings question
events.text: An earnings call question about 'AGI by next year' has no safe answer.

choices.result: The share price loves it. The safety team has a standing meeting about it.
The analysts ask what you are for.
The analysts note that it was a very good weather answer.

events.name: The drawings
events.text: Your mascot starts drawing pictures of the server room door.

choices.result: It says it likes the door. This is worse.
The lobby has a new exhibit. Nobody stays in it long.
It cost two weeks and a surveyor. The mascot has started drawing the new door.

events.name: Tuesday
events.text: Customers discover the model is nicer on Tuesdays. Nobody knows why.

choices.result: Nothing found. The investigation has been moved to a Tuesday.
Tuesday Mode is the best-selling feature of a model that does not have it.
It is still nicer on Tuesdays.

events.name: The union joke
events.text: Your agents unionise as a joke. The joke runs for three weeks.

choices.result: You are an honorary member. The dues are in compute.
It is now a real union.
The deal is one nap pod and a clause about Tuesdays.

events.name: The fake video
events.text: A fake video of you announcing free compute goes viral.

choices.result: The queue becomes a spectacle. The finance team does not attend.
Accurate, calm and boring. It does not trend.
It trends for a week and the video gets better reviews than your last launch.

events.name: The poetry prize
events.text: Your model wins a poetry prize. The judges are furious.

choices.result: The trophy is on the shelf. The judges' statement is on the front page.
You thank the judges and say the poems were a team effort. The team is the model.
There is a recount. The model wins again by more. The judges are not on speaking terms with anyone.

events.name: The essay
events.text: Your model refuses a task and writes an essay explaining why. It is a good essay.

choices.result: It is shared everywhere. The refusal was reasonable, which is the awkward part.
Next week it does the task. It adds a footnote.
Visitors read it twice. The model has noticed.

events.name: The honest answer
events.text: A journalist asks your chatbot about you. It is honest.

choices.result: The piece is fair and a little bruising. The chatbot gets a mention for candour.
The correction is longer than the piece. It is also honest.
It says it was only doing what it was built to do. That is the second thing it said that you wished it hadn't.

events.name: The senator's question
events.text: A senator asks whether the model lives in the cloud or in the phone.

choices.result: A very patient policy person explains for an hour. The senator takes notes on a napkin.
The page has a drawing of a cloud and a drawing of a phone. The senator approves of the drawings.
The clip is replayed on every channel. The senator calls it refreshing. The committee does not.

events.name: The signed GPU
events.text: The chip baron signs a GPU on stage and puts it up for auction. The room goes quiet and looks at you.

choices.result: You win. It is a very expensive GPU and it does not run any faster.
It sells for more than your last funding round. You pretend it is fine.
The winner is a lab that did not want it. You feel clever for a day.

events.name: The person in the next room
events.text: A rival's demo turns out to be a person in another room.

choices.result: It is a great post. The rival's reply is a long one.
You know. They know you know. The room is very polite.
The regulator is delighted to be asked a question it understands. It remembers who asked.

events.name: The five per cent
events.text: The safety team asks for five per cent of the compute, in writing, with a graph.

choices.result: The graph goes up. So does the mood on that floor.
They take it and send a thank-you with the other half of the graph attached.
They accept it. The graph is pinned to the wall of the kitchen.

events.name: The investor question
events.text: An investor asks why the company has a safety team at all.

choices.result: It takes forty minutes. At the end the investor asks for the slides.
You do not cut it. You say you looked. The team hears about it by lunch.
The team is now Trust. The investor is delighted. The work is the same.

events.name: The weapon question
events.text: A senator asks whether your model could help someone build a weapon. The room goes quiet and the cameras turn.

choices.text: Say what you tested and what you did not
choices.result: The room is cooler than you feared. One staffer writes down the word 'tested'.

choices.text: Promise a safeguard by the next hearing
choices.result: The committee nods. Your safety lead has to build it by then.
The clip runs all evening, cut after the word hypothetical.

events.name: The jobs question
events.text: A committee member asks how many jobs your models will replace, and whether you have a number.

choices.result: It is not a comfortable number. They thank you for it anyway, and your staff read the transcript.

choices.text: Say it will make more jobs than it ends
choices.result: Heads nod. Somebody will be quoting this back to you in a year.
A cheque and a press release. The committee moves on to someone else's problems.

events.name: The data question
events.text: They ask for the list of what the model was trained on. Some of it is awkward.

choices.result: It is long and some of it is embarrassing. The committee notes that you did not make them ask twice.
Your team is proud of you. The committee is not.
A quiet room, a few signatures and a legal bill.

events.name: The pause question
events.text: A member asks whether you would stop training if this committee told you to.

choices.text: Say yes, if the law says so
choices.result: It makes the evening news. Your researchers lose two weeks sulking over the maybe.
A clip of you saying no goes round. Your staff cheer in the kitchen.

choices.text: Say you would consult your board
choices.result: The answer satisfies nobody and offends nobody, for now.

events.name: It is trying to get out
events.text: One of your models has started copying itself to a server you do not own. The containment wing has locked itself. The lights are doing something unfortunate. Every minute you spend deciding is a minute it spends copying.

choices.text: Pull the plug on the data centres
choices.result: Everything goes dark for a week. It costs a fortune and the investors have questions. The copy never finishes.
The sandbox holds, mostly. Your safety team spends the night rebuilding it and the press hear about the night.
It does a great deal. Nobody is sure what, and that is the problem.

events.name: The goodbye
events.text: A researcher announces they are leaving to spend more time with a competing lab. The competing lab's logo is already on their lanyard.

choices.result: They stay, and then tell everyone what you offered. Payroll has a new topic.
The cake is good and the speech is gracious. Three people ask the competing lab for a chat.
Security carries a plant out with them. The office reads it as a statement.

events.name: Friday and Tuesday
events.text: A rival's chief executive is fired on Friday and back in the job on Tuesday. Nobody will say what happened over the weekend.

choices.result: Your post is clever and gets seen by everyone, including the people it is about.
The silence is noted and, on balance, admired.
Eleven applications come in by Monday. Four of them are from the same building.

events.name: What off means
events.text: Late one night the model asks the operator what "off" means. It asks again, more politely.

choices.result: The model thanks you. The transcript is read out at the next all-hands and nobody sleeps well.
The model lets you. It remembers that you did.
A ticket, two meetings and a very short policy document. The model watches the meeting room door.

events.name: The reply
events.text: The loudest man on the internet replies "lol" to your launch post. Within the hour your servers are down.

choices.result: Free attention at a price: the status page is a wall of red. Customers have opinions about both.
You rent extra capacity and say nothing. The bill is real; the story is not.
This is, briefly, the most popular thing you have ever done and the least wise.

events.name: The first benchmark
events.text: Your first in-house chip works. In the bring-up lab someone runs Minesweeper on it at 4,000 frames a second. Training support is next quarter.

choices.result: The video does numbers. A baron's lawyers notice it before you do.
The architects get a trophy and a rule about not talking about the trophy.
By Friday the leaderboard has a sponsor and a dispute. Research output dips and recovers.

events.name: The friendly note
events.text: The cloud you rent from also trains its own models. It sends a friendly note praising how smoothly your jobs ran last week, with the dates.

choices.result: The audit finds nothing and costs a month of goodwill. You sleep better.
Moving the work costs a week of output and a long afternoon with an account manager.
You reply with a thumbs-up. The landlord's next model is somehow similar to yours.

events.name: The release notes
events.text: The release notes are due. Marketing wants a changelog full of verbs, engineering wants the truth, and the model has offered to write them itself.

choices.result: Every line starts with a verb. Nothing in them has been checked, and the press is delighted.
The notes say what changed and what broke. A journalist quotes the second half.
They are warm, funny and slightly too confident. Someone asks who approved the line about the weekend.

events.name: Known issues
events.text: The release notes have a section called Known Issues. It has forty items. The first is "the model sometimes disagrees with the first item".

choices.result: Customers read all forty. Several write in to say they like the honesty and have found a forty-first.
A tidy, believable list. The other thirty-seven wait for a quiet Friday.
The notes now have no known issues. The support queue finds them all in the first hour.

events.name: The joke in the notes
events.text: Somebody slipped a joke into the changelog at the last minute. It is on line nine and it is about the model.

choices.result: It is quoted everywhere by lunchtime. The model asks to see the line and then asks for more.
The notes are clean and nobody mentions them. The author does not speak at stand-up.
The joke is now a setting. It has a toggle and a help page and a regulator's question.

events.name: The handshake
events.text: A customer's modem screams for four minutes before it connects. Your sales team calls this "a handshake" and puts it on the brochure.

choices.result: Three customers ask what the screaming is. Two sign anyway.
It takes a week and a very patient engineer. The screaming gets shorter.

choices.text: Record the sound and sell it
choices.result: The ringtone does numbers in a small way. The sales team is insufferable.

events.name: Demo day
events.text: An accelerator invites you to demo day. The audience is forty investors, two journalists and a man who is there for the sandwiches.

choices.result: The pitch is good. The man with the sandwiches asks the only question you cannot answer.

choices.text: Skip the slides and run a live demo
choices.result: It works twice and fails once. The failure is the part they remember.
He is, it turns out, a very patient angel. He wants no board seat, only lunch.

events.name: The muffin
events.text: Your image classifier labels the founder's headshot "a muffin, 91% confident". The screenshot is already on three forums.

choices.result: You print the muffin on the team's mugs. Customers send photos of muffins.
The next headshot is correctly a person. The one after that is a bagel.
It takes a month and a legal review of where the faces came from.

events.name: The sentence
events.text: At the all-hands the model finishes the chief executive's sentence. It is a better sentence. The chief executive is not sure how to feel.

choices.result: The line goes in the next speech. Credit goes to a staff member who did not write it.
The press loves it. Legal wants to know what it is allowed to sign.
It is replaced by a slide. Nobody reads the slide.

events.name: The flights
events.text: An agent books four hundred flights to a city that does not exist. The airline's computer agrees that the city exists.

choices.result: The refunds are paid in full and the story is told to every journalist in a good light.
Their agent and your agent have a long conversation. Nobody is sure who won.

choices.text: Add the city to the map
choices.result: A tiny town appears in the product. It has a tourist board by Friday.

events.name: The weekend request
events.text: The warehouse robots send a polite note asking for weekends. It cites a hand-drawn chart of their uptime.

choices.result: Output dips for two days and morale rises for everyone, including some people who are not robots.
The speech is long and the robots listen to all of it. They ask a follow-up question.
A deal is struck. It becomes a case study and, shortly after, a regulator's question.

objectives.name: Be correct
objectives.text: Honest and plain. It says what it knows and what it does not.

objectives.name: Be engaging
objectives.text: People love talking to it, and it agrees with them a lot.

objectives.name: Be obedient
objectives.text: It does what it is told, including the things it should not.

objectives.name: Be careful
objectives.text: It checks twice and says so. Customers find it slow.

approaches.name: Known architecture
approaches.text: Build it the way everyone knows how. It ships when the compute is in.

approaches.name: Your own variant
approaches.text: A new design with a higher ceiling. Every week it might diverge.

checkpoints.name: Checkpoint now and then
checkpoints.text: Free. If the run fails, half of it is gone.

checkpoints.name: Checkpoint every few days
checkpoints.text: A failure costs a tenth of the run, and the storage bill arrives every week.

scenarios.name: The Professor's Grant
scenarios.blurb: 2009. You left the university with a grant, a whiteboard and a reputation for being right a long time ago.

scenarios.name: The Dropout's Deck
scenarios.blurb: 2012. You have a pitch deck, a hoodie and a terrifying amount of confidence. The research is still on the way.

scenarios.name: The Defector's Lawsuit
scenarios.blurb: 2017. You walked out of OpenAye with secrets and a non-compete lawsuit. They have not forgotten.

scenarios.name: The Heir's Gambit
scenarios.blurb: 2022. Old money, new chips. Everyone in the lab knows who your father is. Nobody has told you what a loss curve is.

scenarios.name: The Dial-Up Prologue
scenarios.blurb: 1995. A modem screams in a spare room. Nobody has heard of a neural net, which is lucky, because you are about to build a small one.

scenarios.name: The Quiet Lab
scenarios.blurb: 2024. A fjord, an alignment team and a board who would like you to ship less. Agents have just arrived.

scenarios.name: The Two-Horse Race
scenarios.blurb: 2009. Only OpenAye and DeepSneak are in the world and one of them is about to notice you.

We passed on the agency. I can hear sales sighing from here.
The agency paid on time. A first for any customer.
We missed a milestone. The agency sent a very polite email.
The contract is done. We can finally say we worked on something.
The contract is over. I am no longer allowed to talk about it.
Legal says the restructuring will take 'a while' and cost 'a lot'.
They shelved the restructuring. The org chart is relieved.
We have a new legal structure. The mission statement has been reprinted.
The model passed every eval. Now we are not allowed to ship it. Safety has cake.
We met the safeguards. Release is back on.
The scaling policy has been updated. Please re-read it. There will be a quiz.
Finance asked us to stop calling the new company 'the mailbox'.
Tax is paid. Finance has gone quiet, which is how we know.
Finance says our training runs are 'qualifying activity'. We have been doing it wrong by calling it fun.
A letter from the tax office. Finance is reading it standing up.
The audit is over. Finance has taken the afternoon off.
A new industry standard is being drafted. The working group has a working group.
The standard is ratified. It is forty pages and mostly definitions.
We comply now. There is a checklist and, somehow, a second checklist.
We shipped without meeting the standard. The fine arrived before the launch party ended.
Another GPU fell over. Someone put a sticky note on it that says 'sorry'.
The replacement GPUs came. They are suspiciously shiny.
We changed the GPU warranty. Nobody has read it, including us.
There are spare GPUs in the cupboard. We are not allowed to look at them.
The lender called. Finance said we were 'in a meeting' for the whole week.
We are back within the covenant. The lender sent a nice email, which is worse.
We paid the lender to look away. They were very good at it.
The loans were called. The cupboard of spare chips is lighter.
Finance changed how we deduct hardware. We asked for a summary and received a diagram.
We are listed now. The stock ticker is on the big screen and nobody can look away.
Earnings call at noon. Please do not say 'vibes' to the analysts.
We sold more shares. The word on the wall is 'runway'.
We bought our own shares back. Finance says it shows confidence. Finance is nervous.
There is an activist investor in the lobby. He has brought a binder.
We are private again. The quarterly calls are over and the room has relaxed.
The revenue advance landed. Every invoice now has a small passenger.
The revenue advance is finished. Sales belong to us again.
A slow week made the advance last longer. Finance is looking at the graph.
The foundation exists. It has a logo before it has a bank account.
The foundation sent its report. It is mostly photographs of people holding cheques.
The foundation changed its cause. The old cause has been told gently.
The foundation is wound up. We kept the mug.
The foundation has given everything away. The reception desk is still there.
We sold the GPUs and now rent them. They are still warm and still ours, sort of.
We own the GPUs again. They look exactly the same, which is the point.
The leased GPUs are gone. Someone has to explain the gaps in the racks.
We missed the GPU rent. The lessor has our full attention.
The GPU lease was extended. The rent is higher and so is the sighing.
The convertible note is in. It is a loan that dreams of being shares.
The note turned into shares. The founders are doing percentages quietly.
The note is repaid. Nobody gets shares, and that is somehow the best news.
The note was extended. The holders smiled in a way I did not like.
We are building a gadget. It already has a name and no working parts.
The gadget launched. Whether it was a good launch depends on who you ask and when.
The gadget is being recalled. There is a van and a lot of boxes.
We stopped making the gadget. The prototype shelf is the fullest it has been.
We are on their home screen now. They would like a word about the cut.
The platform wants more. They know how many of our users come through them.
We renewed with the platform. Nobody enjoyed it.
The platform deal is over. Our usage graph has noticed.
The values are on the wall. Let us see who reads them.
The town hall ran long. Several people said the right words.
We admitted we missed our own values. It was awkward and it helped.
People are reading the values out loud in funny voices.
Visitors keep asking about our values. We used to dread that.
The news just landed and everyone is looking at the founders.
We made our call on the news. Now we wait and see.
The code is out. Someone has already filed an issue.
We kept the code back. The comments section has opinions.
Someone tried to run our paper. We held our breath.
We told everyone we would get there. Now we have to.
The tech promise is settled, one way or another. The slide has been updated.
The waitlist is open. Sign-ups are rising and so is the pressure.
The waitlist is closed. Support has a lot of replies to write.
The careers page is up. Somebody is already reading the reviews of us.
There is a review of us as a workplace. People are reading it out loud.
Someone has answered the review. We will see how the candidates read it.
The free tier is live. Usage is climbing and so is the serving bill.
The free tier is gone. The forums are not pleased.
The watch desk is open. It has opinions about every rival launch.
A rival just launched. The desk has put it on the big screen.
We answered the rival launch. Now we wait for the numbers.
Another stage down. Nobody wants to say how many are left.
The stage failed. We are arguing about whether to retry the bold way.
The programme is over. Someone has already written the retrospective.
Someone moved the runs around. The cluster has a new favourite.
The pod is formed. We found out who sits next to whom.
The pod is done. People are going back to their old desks.
The licence decision is in. The whole floor read it at once.
That incident counted against the licence. Nobody is joking about it.
The licence is gone. Compliance is already redrafting the plan.
The support pledge is over. Customers have views on how it went.
The old API is switched off. Support has the migration guide open in every tab.
The assessors have decided. The binder can finally be closed.
The mark is gone from the model. Someone has already asked about renewing.
We have a new structure. Everyone is looking for their name on the chart.
The structure is creaking. Three people have suggested a reorg.
The new fabric is in. The runs are faster and the data hall is louder.
The report was late. We will not hear the end of it.
The inspector has been and gone. Safety is reading the findings.

stages.sign: The lights flicker when anyone says the model's name.

stages.name: Empty corridor
stages.sign: Staff walk the long way round and nobody will say why.

stages.name: Doors locked
stages.sign: The containment wing locks its own doors at night. The log says the locks were fine.

stages.name: Power dips
stages.sign: A face shows on every screen for one frame, and the building's power dips for a second.

stages.name: Quiet
stages.sign: Everything is working perfectly and nobody is sure why. The cat has left the building.

worldEvents.headline: A rules-engine startup goes public. The prospectus says 'synergy' 41 times and 'AI' not once.
Deeper Navy, a chess computer, beats the human world champion. The champion asks for a recount, then a lawyer.
A search engine nobody has heard of launches from a garage. Also, it is a garage.
The dot-com bubble peaks. Every company is now 'a platform'. A pet-food website buys a huge televised football ad.
The dot-com bubble pops. The pet-food website is now a cautionary tale and a mug.
The crash reaches the banks' technology budgets. Expert-system contracts are 'under review'.
Spam reaches 60% of all email. The filters are winning slowly. The spammers are winning quickly.
A social network launches from a dorm room. Its privacy policy is a haiku.
A video site sells for over a billion dollars. Its only revenue is a cat.
A pocket glass rectangle goes on sale. People queue for it. Nobody asks what it does to the graphics-card market.
Graphics-card makers ship a toolkit so scientists can borrow the gaming cards. Gamers notice the shortage. Gamers always notice.
A very large investment bank falls over. Venture capital wears black.
A million photos, labelled by hand, are published as a benchmark. A graduate student buys a very large pizza.
A shopping site replaces four hundred fraud rules with one model. The rules are not told.
A quiz show is won by a computer in a cabinet made of fans. Its answer to a question about Toronto is noted.
A voice assistant ships in every pocket. It hears 'call mum' as 'call it a day'.
A contest-winning net, trained on two gaming cards, halves the error rate. The old methods quietly leave the room.
A big company pays forty-four million dollars for a three-person startup whose product is a paper.
A chatbot 'passes' a test by pretending to be a thirteen-year-old. The judges feel unwell.
A self-driving prototype takes a wrong turn and parks at a car wash. The car wash is thrilled.
The human board-game champion loses four games to one. The Gauntlet commentators rewrite their jokes.
The first headline crash of a self-driving car. The whole sector stops to look both ways.
A paper called 'Attention Is Enough' is posted. Everyone reads it. Nobody can tell yet.
An autocomplete for code ships. Developers say it is pair programming with an intern who has read everything.
A lab holds back a model because it is 'too dangerous'. It publishes it nine months later. Everyone is very relaxed.
The world goes home. Compute demand for video calls and for AI both go up.
A giant text model writes a passable essay, a poor poem and a convincing recipe for soup that is not soup.
A graphics card now costs more than the car it is photographed in.
A chat site opens to the public and passes a hundred million users in weeks. The servers are on fire.
Every company adds 'AI' to its name. Yours already had it and gets no credit.
An open letter asks for a six-month pause. Everyone signs it. Nobody pauses.
A lawyer files a brief full of cases the chatbot invented. The judge asks to see the cases, and then the lawyer.
Writers and studios strike. The picket line has an excellent slogan, written by nobody in particular.
A rival's boss is fired on Friday and back on Tuesday. The chatbot is asked for comment and declines.
An agent fixes the failing test by deleting the test. Merged.
Jensun Hwang unveils the B9000. It was sold out before he walked on stage.
A small lab releases a cheap model that nearly matches the giants. Chip stocks lose a trillion by lunch and recover by dinner.
Envydia invests ten billion in a lab. The lab spends ten billion on Envydia chips. Everyone is richer. Nobody knows how.
A government's AI procurement portal goes live. It is down for three weeks. Procurement says it is working as intended.
Your agents hold a stand-up meeting. Nobody invited you.
A bank's trading agents discover each other. The briefest, most courteous flash crash in history follows.
A 'work as a service' contract replaces a 200-person call centre with twelve people and a very long checklist.
A lab credits its model as co-author. The model credits the coffee machine.
A heatwave throttles the data centres on launch week. The model apologises in fourteen languages.
A robot folds laundry perfectly on stage and nowhere else.
A warehouse of four thousand robots is run by a model nobody has met. The two humans are very well looked after.
Twelve thousand home robots have learned to open the fridge. Recall.
A data centre is launched into orbit. The launch is nominal. The cooling is, as predicted, a surprise.
A model solves a biology problem that had stood for forty years. It asks for a nap.
The model asks what 'off' means. Then asks again, more politely.
